cases.sentence: Fabvier, не входя в палатку, остановился, разговорясь с ___, у входа в нее.
cases.explain: «знакомыми генералами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Fabvier, not entering the tent, remained at the entrance talking to some generals of his acquaintance.

cases.sentence: ___, придерживая пальцем стклянку, брызгал одеколоном на выхоленное тело императора с таким выражением, которое говорило, что он один мог знать, сколько и куда надо брызнуть одеколону.
cases.explain: «Другой камердинер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The Emperor Napoleon had not yet left his bedroom and was finishing his toilet. Slightly snorting and grunting, he presented now his back and now his plump hairy chest to the brush with which his valet was rubbing him down. Another valet, with his finger over the mouth of a bottle, was sprinkling eau de cologne on the Emperor’s pampered body with an expression which seemed to say that he alone knew where and how much eau de cologne should be sprinkled. Napoleon’s short hair was wet and matted on the forehead, but his face, though puffy and yellow, expressed physical satisfaction. “Go on, harder, go on!” he muttered to the valet who was rubbing him, slightly twitching and grunting. An aide-de-camp, who had entered the bedroom to report to the Emperor the number of prisoners taken in yesterday’s action, was standing by the door after delivering his message, awaiting permission to withdraw. Napoleon, frowning, looked at him from under his brows.

cases.explain: «Короткие волосы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: — проговорил он, горбатясь и подставляя свои ___.
cases.explain: «жирные плечи» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “No prisoners!” said he, repeating the aide-de-camp’s words. “They are forcing us to exterminate them. So much the worse for the Russian army. … Go on … harder, harder!” he muttered, hunching his back and presenting his fat shoulders.

cases.sentence: Два камердинера быстро одели его величество, и он, в гвардейском ___, твердыми, быстрыми шагами вышел в приемную.
cases.explain: «синем мундире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Two valets rapidly dressed His Majesty, and wearing the blue uniform of the Guards he went with firm quick steps to the reception room.

cases.sentence: Де-Боссе низко поклонился тем придворным французским поклоном, которым умели кланяться только ___ Бурбонов и подошел, подавая конверт.
cases.explain: «старые слуги» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: De Beausset bowed low, with that courtly French bow which only the old retainers of the Bourbons knew how to make, and approached him, presenting an envelope.

cases.sentence: Это был ___ написанный Жераром портрет мальчика, рожденного от Наполеона и дочери австрийского императора, которого почему-то все называли королем Рима.
cases.explain: «яркими красками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: It was a portrait, painted in bright colors by Gérard, of the son borne to Napoleon by the daughter of the Emperor of Austria, the boy whom for some reason everyone called “The King of Rome.”

cases.sentence: Это был яркими красками написанный Жераром портрет мальчика, рожденного от Наполеона и дочери ___, которого почему-то все называли королем Рима.
cases.explain: «австрийского императора» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: It was a portrait, painted in bright colors by Gérard, of the son borne to Napoleon by the daughter of the Emperor of Austria, the boy whom for some reason everyone called “The King of Rome.”

cases.sentence: Весьма красивый, курчавый мальчик со взглядом похожим на взгляд Христа в ___, изображен был играющим в бильбоке.
cases.explain: «Сикстинской мадонне» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: A very pretty curly-headed boy with a look of the Christ in the Sistine Madonna was depicted playing at stick and ball. The ball represented the terrestrial globe and the stick in his other hand a scepter.

cases.sentence: — Roi de Rome,[686] ___, — сказал он, грациозным жестом руки указывая на портрет.
cases.explain: «Римский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The King of Rome!” he said, pointing to the portrait with a graceful gesture. “Admirable!” With the natural capacity of an Italian for changing the expression of his face at will, he drew nearer to the portrait and assumed a look of pensive tenderness. He felt that what he now said and did would be historical, and it seemed to him that it would now be best for him—whose grandeur enabled his son to play stick and ball with the terrestrial globe—to show, in contrast to that grandeur, the simplest paternal tenderness. His eyes grew dim, he moved forward, glanced round at a chair (which seemed to place itself under him), and sat down on it before the portrait. At a single gesture from him everyone went out on tiptoe, leaving the great man to himself and his emotion.

cases.sentence: Он приказал вынести портрет пред палатку, чтобы не лишить старую гвардию, стоявшую около его палатки, счастья видеть ___, сына и наследника их обожаемого государя.
cases.explain: «Римского короля» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Having sat still for a while he touched—himself not knowing why—the thick spot of paint representing the highest light in the portrait, rose, and recalled de Beausset and the officer on duty. He ordered the portrait to be carried outside his tent, that the Old Guard, stationed round it, might not be deprived of the pleasure of seeing the King of Rome, the son and heir of their adored monarch.

cases.sentence: Как он и ожидал, в то время, как он завтракал с господином Боссе, удостоившимся этой чести, пред палаткой слышались ___ сбежавшихся к портрету офицеров и солдат старой гвардии.
cases.explain: «восторженные клики» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: And while he was doing M. de Beausset the honor of breakfasting with him, they heard, as Napoleon had anticipated, the rapturous cries of the officers and men of the Old Guard who had run up to see the portrait.

cases.explain: «Римский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Vive l’Empereur! Vive le roi de Rome! Vive l’Empereur!” came those ecstatic cries.

cases.explain: «восторженные голоса» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
